notes: DRIFT is in the shape of `options`, not its presence: the declared 200 schema types data.options as a bare array (`{type:'array', items:{type:'object'}}`), but with fetch_options=true the live response returns data.options as an OBJECT — {data:[...30 rows...], info:{page,page_size,count:50,prev,next:2}} — not an array. Code written against the declared contract (`data.options.map(...)`) would throw; the real array is one level deeper at data.options.data, and there is a full second, wholly undocumented pagination surface (options.info) alongside the one the guidance does describe for linked_projects. Everything else matched the declared contract exactly: both path ids required as positive ints, fetch_options/​p query params behaved as documented, data.{id,link_to_future_projects,linked_project_count,linked_to_all_projects,linked_projects} all present and correctly nested under data, and linked_projects (1 item, well under the fixed 30-page-size) needed no paging to verify. Single attempt, no retries needed (200 on the first call). Route identification for the routing-eval note: this capability's own path is `/api/v1/admin-v2/settings/custom-fields/{custom_fields_id}/datasets/{dataset_id}` — clearly the admin/workspace-settings surface (same family as get_custom_field_definition_v2, list_custom_field_dataset_options_v2, list_workspace_fields_v2), not the public TestCase-only surface (list_custom_fields_v2, get_custom_field_v2, get_custom_field_values_v1). But the capability NAME alone doesn't signal that: unlike get_custom_field_definition_v2, this one carries no '_definition_' token, so the naming heuristic from the routing eval doesn't fully generalize. Worse, get_custom_field_v2 (the public-ish field read) hands back a ready-made `dataset_urls` hint of `/api/v2/custom-fields/105915/datasets/31196` — a different path/version than the admin-v2 route actually used here — so following that in-response hint would lead a caller to the wrong surface entirely. The only reliable signal is the path declared by describeCapability itself (the admin-v2/settings/custom-fields segment), not the capability's name and not any URL the API hands back in a sibling response.
